question: What is the name of the thick muscular layer that forms the walls of the heart?
explanation: The myocardium is the thick, muscular middle layer of the heart made of cardiac muscle tissue that pumps blood. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why does heart muscle need to work continuously without resting periods?

options.A: To prevent the heart valves from closing too tightly during systole
options.B: To maintain continuous blood flow and oxygen delivery to the body
options.C: To store extra glucose reserves for sudden bursts of physical activity
options.D: To generate electrical impulses that travel independently of the brain

explanation: Body organs constantly require oxygen and nutrients, so the heart must pump blood uninterrupted every second. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h1)

question: How many nuclei are typically found in a normal adult heart muscle cell?

options.B: Two distinct nuclei at the cell poles

explanation: Unlike skeletal muscle cells which have many nuclei, heart muscle cells generally feature a single nucleus right in the center. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which cell part is found in very high numbers inside heart muscle cells to supply constant energy?
explanation: Heart muscle cells need massive amounts of energy to keep beating, which is why they are packed with mitochondria. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the main job of gap junctions in the heart muscle?

options.A: Allowing free passage of ions for rapid electrical communication between cells
options.B: Anchoring the actin and myosin filaments directly to the cell membrane
options.C: Secreting hormones that regulate overall systemic blood pressure
options.D: Providing strong mechanical anchorage to prevent cells from tearing apart

explanation: Gap junctions create pathways for electrical signals to spread swiftly from cell to cell across the heart wall. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h3)

question: What would happen to the heart if desmosomes were missing from the cell connections?

options.A: The heart would stop producing adenosine triphosphate completely
options.B: Muscle cells could pull apart from each other during powerful contractions
options.C: Blood would flow backward through the chambers without hindrance
options.D: Electrical signals would travel too slowly to coordinate a proper heartbeat

explanation: Desmosomes act as physical spot-welds holding adjacent cells tightly together when the heart contracts strongly. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why is a long refractory period important for normal heart function?

options.A: It prevents tetanus and allows the heart chambers to refill with blood
options.B: It speeds up the rate of cellular respiration inside the mitochondria
options.C: It stops the nervous system from sending voluntary signals to the myocardium
options.D: It ensures that potassium ions remain trapped inside the sarcoplasmic reticulum

explanation: A longer resting phase ensures the heart muscle relaxes fully between beats, preventing continuous cramping. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h4)

question: Besides internal storage, where else does heart muscle get calcium to trigger contraction?

options.A: Breakdown of glycogen granules stored within the sarcoplasm
options.B: Active transport pumps located on the outer nuclear membrane
options.C: Extracellular fluid entering through channels in the cell membrane
options.D: Direct absorption from the red blood cells flowing inside the chamber

explanation: Heart tissue relies heavily on calcium entering from outside the cell to help trigger internal muscle contraction. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which structure acts as the natural pacemaker of a healthy human heart?
explanation: The sinoatrial node fires electrical impulses at the highest baseline frequency, setting the normal heart rate. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h5)

question: What property allows specific heart cells to generate electrical impulses without nerve signals?
explanation: Automaticity is the specialized ability of certain heart cells to start electrical impulses on their own without brain stimulation. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the main energy pathway used by healthy heart muscle tissue?
explanation: Heart muscle cells rely almost exclusively on oxygen-dependent pathways to generate the steady energy needed for constant beating. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why does a sudden blockage in a coronary artery quickly damage the heart muscle?

options.A: Coronary arteries do not connect to gap junctions or intercalated discs
options.B: Cardiac muscle cells lack the ability to switch fuel sources during emergencies
options.C: The heart extracts almost all available oxygen at rest, leaving no reserve capacity
options.D: The tissue relies entirely on anaerobic metabolism under normal daily conditions

explanation: Because the resting heart already uses most of the oxygen delivered to it, it cannot pull extra oxygen when blood flow drops. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h6)

question: How does damaged heart muscle tissue typically heal after a severe heart attack?

options.A: Hypertrophy of smooth muscle layers lining the coronary blood vessels
options.B: Rapid regeneration of new, healthy cardiomyocytes from nearby stem cells
options.C: Complete electrical restoration via regeneration of damaged gap junctions
options.D: Replacement with fibrous scar tissue rather than functional muscle cells

explanation: Adult heart muscle cannot easily repair itself, so dead muscle cells are replaced by non-contractile scar tissue. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal responsibility when monitoring a patient's heart status in clinical practice?

options.A: Monitoring laboratory results for abnormal potassium and calcium levels
options.B: Surgically repairing damaged coronary arteries at the bedside
options.C: Screening for physical signs of chest discomfort or respiratory distress
options.D: Assessing vital signs and tracking trends in maternal blood pressure

explanation: Bedside surgery on coronary arteries is performed by specialized surgeons in an operating theatre, not as a general nursing task. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h7)
